verses.1: And it was in the days of Ahaz, who ruled from Huldah to Kish, seventy and ten years.
verses.2: In those days, when Ahaz became king over his kingdom, which was located in the capital city of Samaria.
verses.3: In the sixth year of his reign, he prepared food for all his servants and officials. He also distributed gifts and rewards to those who served him.
verses.4: In his sight, there is nothing but the glory of his kingdom and the riches of his grandeur. For many days, he remains in that state.
verses.5: And during these days, the king made a feast for all the people who were found in the royal palace. Everyone, from the smallest to the greatest, was allowed to eat seven days in the courtyard of the king’s house.
verses.6: Chur’karpas and Tekeleth Ahuz are placed on the beams of the bow. Argaman is also placed along the silver rails. There are also statues of six hands, made of gold and silver, on the surface of the Hat-Washesh. And there’s also Dar and Soharet.
verses.7: And the cups were made of gold, along with various other utensils. There was also a great deal of wine from the royal treasury, just like what the king had.
verses.8: And when a law is established, no one can change it. For that is what the king does: he establishes laws for every household, so that each person may do as they wish.
verses.9: And even the queen made a drink for the women in the royal palace, which was intended for King Ahşverosh.
verses.10: On the seventh day, it was good in the king’s heart. In that day, he said to Mehuman, “In Zethona, Barhona, Abagtha, Zethar, and Karkas, seven days passed during which the guards stood before the king, Ahşverosh.”
verses.11: To bring the queen before the king, in a royal coffin, so that all people and officials might see her beauty. For she is truly beautiful.
verses.12: The queen became angry and refused to listen to the king’s words, which were given by the scribes. The king became extremely angry, and his anger grew even more.
verses.13: And the king said to the wise men, “Know, you who understand the times, that this is what the king wants to say before all those who understand religion and law.”
verses.14: And those who approached him were Karshna, Shetar Admata, Tarsish Merres, Mersnana, and Memukan Shiv’at Shari. They were also Pares and Madai, those who could see the faces of the kings who sat at the head of the kingdom.
verses.15: What should be done in the kingdom? And what about those who did not follow the commands of King Ahšweros, as ordered by the priests.
verses.16: And he said to the king and to the officials, “It is not just the king alone who suffers. The queen also suffers, because all the officials and all the people in the kingdoms of Ahşverosh are suffering.”
verses.17: For the king’s command went forth against all women, so that they would be destroyed by their own eyes. The king, Ahşverosh, ordered that the queen’s concubines should be brought before him. But they did not come.
verses.18: And today, we shall say that the women of Parshumadai heard what the queen said to all the king’s wives. And it happened in that same moment of anger and indignation.
verses.19: If there is good upon the king, then things related to his reign will go well ahead of him. They will be recorded in the laws and regulations. But if there is no good, then Ahshverosh will not allow anything to happen. The king will give her a bad kingdom instead.
verses.20: And we heard the words of the king, who did everything he could in his kingdom. It was a great kingdom, and all the women gave their beloved husbands things precious, both large and small.
verses.21: And this pleased the king and the nobles. So the king did as he was told.
verses.22: And he sent letters to all the kingdoms of the kings. To each kingdom, according to its own writing, and to each people, according to their own language. So that everyone could speak in their own language in their own home.
